+## 9. Shared complete contexts and a spectral discrepancy bound
+
+**Definition 9.1 (Unnormalized context weights and spectral tails).** Retain exactly $B_n$, $K_m^{a,b}$, $\mathcal D_K$, $\mathscr F_{N,n}^{0,0}$ and $\mathscr R_{N,n}$ from Definitions 1.1–1.3. Let $p$ be band-compatible on $B_n$, and let $C=[c,d]$ be an interior interval, so $1<c\le d<n$ and $m=d-c+1$. A complete complement is $\eta=(u,v)$ with $u=W_{[1,c-1]}$ and $v=W_{[d+1,n]}$. For each extendible $\eta$ write
+
+$$
+p_\eta=p(W_{C^c}=\eta)>0,\qquad
+p_C^\eta(w)=p(W_C=w\mid W_{C^c}=\eta),\qquad
+a=u_{c-1},\quad b=v_1.
+\tag{9.1}
+$$
+
+Here and below $C^c$ in a finite-word conditional means $[1,n]\setminus C$. Let $S_C^{a,b}(p)$ have one row for every extendible complete complement with these adjacent bits, one column for every $w\in K_m^{a,b}$, and entries
+
+$$
+S_C^{a,b}(p)(\eta,w)=\sqrt{p_\eta}\,p_C^\eta(w).
+\tag{9.2}
+$$
+
+The mass $p_\eta$ is not divided by $p(W_{c-1}=a,W_{d+1}=b)$. In particular, the four matrices retain their original relative weights. A type without rows gives the zero matrix. For a finite real matrix $S$ and integer $q\ge0$ put
+
+$$
+\operatorname{tail}_q(S)=\sum_{j>q}\sigma_j(S)^2,\qquad
+c_m=\frac{6^{-4m}}{2m},
+\tag{9.3}
+$$
+
+where singular values are decreasing and continued by zeros.
+
+**Theorem 9.2 (Weighted shared-context lower bound).** For every $N\ge1$, every band-compatible $p$ on $B_n$, and every deterministic family of disjoint nonempty interior intervals $C_j$,
+
+$$
+\mathscr R_{N,n}(p)\ge
+\sum_j c_{|C_j|}\sum_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}
+\operatorname{tail}_{N^2}\bigl(S_{C_j}^{a,b}(p)\bigr).
+\tag{9.4}
+$$
+
+Every comparison in the minimum on the left is one global $r\in\mathscr F_{N,n}^{0,0}$. All conditionals and weights on the right belong to the same $p$.
+
+Proof. Fix such an $r$ and one interval $C=[c,d]$. Extend its word probabilities by zero to the whole binary cube, as in (1.7). The ordinary ranks at the cuts $c-1$ and $d$ are at most $N$, since ordinary rank is at most nonnegative rank. At the first cut choose $h\le N$ prefix rows indexed by $u_\alpha$ spanning all prefix rows. There are real coefficients $A_\alpha(u)$, independent of $w,v$, such that
+
+$$
+r(uwv)=\sum_{\alpha=1}^h A_\alpha(u)r(u_\alpha wv).
+\tag{9.5}
+$$
+
+At the second cut choose a basis $D_\beta(v)$, $1\le\beta\le e\le N$, for the row space of the prefix/suffix matrix. For each $\alpha,w$ there are coefficients $H_{\alpha\beta}(w)$ with
+
+$$
+r(u_\alpha wv)=\sum_{\beta=1}^e H_{\alpha\beta}(w)D_\beta(v),\qquad
+r(uwv)=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}A_\alpha(u)D_\beta(v)H_{\alpha\beta}(w).
+\tag{9.6}
+$$
+
+Thus the matrix with rows $(u,v)$, columns $w$ and entries $r(uwv)$ has ordinary rank at most $he\le N^2$. These equalities hold on the full binary cube, including every illegal entry. The auxiliary real coefficients need not be nonnegative. This is the two-cut linear-factorization mechanism also underlying the context rank in [Intrinsic, §2][SC-I]; it is used only as a necessary condition on the given global $r$.
+
+Both $p$ and $r$ are positive on $B_n$ by Definition 1.3. Hence every extendible complement has $r_\eta=r(W_{C^c}=\eta)>0$. For a fixed adjacent-bit type define
+
+$$
+T_C^{a,b}(\eta,w)=\sqrt{p_\eta}\,r_C^\eta(w),\qquad
+r_C^\eta(w)=\frac{r(uwv)}{r_\eta}.
+\tag{9.7}
+$$
+
+Restricting the matrix in (9.6) to those rows and to $K_m^{a,b}$, then scaling row $\eta$ by $\sqrt{p_\eta}/r_\eta$, gives $T_C^{a,b}$. Consequently its ordinary rank is at most $N^2$. For every such row, $p_C^\eta$ and $r_C^\eta$ are band-compatible on exactly the same $K_m^{a,b}$: each insertion inequality is an original inequality divided by the corresponding fixed positive complement mass.
+
+The global single-site predictors at sites in $C$, after the entire complement is fixed, are exactly the single-site predictors of these conditional block laws. Disintegration, [Guarded, Lemma 8.1][SC-G] and $\|x\|_1\ge\|x\|_2$ give
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\sum_{i\in C}\mathbb E_p(p_i(W_{-i})-r_i(W_{-i}))^2
+&=\sum_\eta p_\eta\mathcal D_{K_m^{a,b}}(p_C^\eta\Vert r_C^\eta)\\
+&\ge c_m\sum_\eta p_\eta\|p_C^\eta-r_C^\eta\|_1^2\\
+&\ge c_m\sum_{a,b}\|S_C^{a,b}(p)-T_C^{a,b}\|_F^2.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{9.8}
+$$
+
+In the first two sums $a,b$ are the adjacent bits of that $\eta$. Forced fibers have zero single-site discrepancy; singleton completion sets satisfy the same inequality. Nonextendible complements contribute zero and require no denominator.
+
+The needed low-rank approximation inequality is the classical orthogonal-projection bound [Eckart–Young][SC-EY], also used in [Whitebox, Theorem 43.5][SC-W]. Explicitly, if $T$ has rank at most $q$ and $Q$ is the orthogonal projection onto its column space, then
+
+$$
+\|S-T\|_F^2\ge\|(I-Q)S\|_F^2
+=\operatorname{tr}(SS^{\mathsf T})-\operatorname{tr}(QSS^{\mathsf T})
+\ge\sum_{j>q}\sigma_j(S)^2.
+\tag{9.9}
+$$
+
+To obtain the last inequality, diagonalize $SS^{\mathsf T}$. The diagonal entries of $Q$ in that basis lie in $[0,1]$ and sum to at most $q$, so their pairing with the decreasing nonnegative eigenvalues is at most the sum of the first $q$. Apply (9.9) to each term of (9.8) with $q=N^2$. The site sums for disjoint $C_j$ are distinct summands of $\mathcal D_{B_n}(p\Vert r)$, even if their complements or adjacent bits overlap. They can therefore be added without independence. Minimize over this single global $r$. If the family is empty its value is $+\infty$, so (9.4) still holds. $\square$
+
+## 10. All finite comparison ranks admit a global/local separation
+
+**Theorem 10.1 (One common stationary law at every comparison rank).** For every integer $N\ge2$, set
+
+$$
+k=N^2+1,\qquad m=2N^2=2(k-1),\qquad
+ a_\ell=\frac13+\frac{\ell-1}{24N^2},\qquad w_\ell=\frac1k,
+\quad 1\le\ell\le k.
+\tag{10.1}
+$$
+
+Use the two-state $A_\ell,\lambda_\ell,D_x$ of (3.2) with these parameters, and define
+
+$$
+M_x^{(N)}=\bigoplus_{\ell=1}^kD_xA_\ell,\qquad
+\lambda^{(N)}=(w_1\lambda_1,\ldots,w_k\lambda_k).
+\tag{10.2}
+$$
+
+This is one element of the original $\Theta_{2k}$. Its actual stationary law is
+
+$$
+P^{(N)}=\sum_{\ell=1}^kw_\ell R^{a_\ell},\qquad
+\mu_n=P^{(N)}_{[1,n]},\qquad
+\mu_n(w)=\lambda^{(N)}M_{w_1}^{(N)}\cdots M_{w_n}^{(N)}\mathbf1
+\quad\text{for every }n.
+\tag{10.3}
+$$
+
+All legal words have positive mass and every $\mu_n$ is band-compatible. Define
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+z_\ell&=\frac{a_\ell}{(1-a_\ell)^2},&
+\rho_\ell&=\frac{a_\ell}{1+a_\ell},&
+\Delta&=\min_{\ell\ne h}|\rho_\ell-\rho_h|>0,\\
+Z_\ell&=\sum_{w\in B_m}z_\ell^{k(w)},&
+v_\ell(w)&=\frac{z_\ell^{k(w)}}{Z_\ell},&
+b_\ell&=\lambda_{\ell,0}(A_\ell^{m+1})_{00}>0,\\
+G&=\sum_{\ell=1}^kw_\ell b_\ell v_\ell v_\ell^{\mathsf T},&
+\gamma&=\lambda_k(G)>0.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{10.4}
+$$
+
+The $v_\ell$ are column probability vectors on $B_m$; $\lambda_{\ell,0}=1/(1+a_\ell)$, and eigenvalues are decreasing. For every $n>m$ with $(n-m)\Delta\ge8$,
+
+$$
+\mathscr R_{N,n}(\mu_n)\ge
+c_m\left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{m}\right\rfloor
+\left[\gamma-4\exp\left(-\frac{(n-m)\Delta^2}{64}\right)\right]_+,
+\qquad [x]_+=\max(x,0).
+\tag{10.5}
+$$
+
+In particular,
+
+$$
+\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\mathscr R_{N,n}(\mu_n)}n
+\ge\frac{c_m\gamma}{m}>0.
+\tag{10.6}
+$$
+
+In contrast, for every fixed $t\ge1$, every $n>t$ with $(n-t)\Delta\ge8$, and every deterministic family of disjoint length-$t$ intervals $C_j\subseteq[1,n]$,
+
+$$
+\sum_j\mathbb E_{\mu_n}\delta_{N,t}^{a_j,b_j}
+\bigl(\mu_n(W_{C_j}=\cdot\mid W_{C_j^c})\bigr)
+\le2n\exp\left(-\frac{(n-t)\Delta^2}{64}\right)\longrightarrow0.
+\tag{10.7}
+$$
+
+The adjacent bits in (10.7) are the actual observed adjacent bits, with zero at an open endpoint as in (1.10).
+
+Proof. The parameters in (10.1) lie in $[1/3,3/8]$ and are distinct. The persistent-mixture construction of Propositions 3.2–3.3 applies to any finite number of positive-weight components: their proofs use only the displayed parameter range, positive weights and block-diagonal matrices. Equivalently, apply those propositions with their component-count parameter equal to $k-1$, then compare against the rank $N$ used here. Each $A_\ell$ is stochastic, $\lambda_\ell A_\ell=\lambda_\ell$ and $(D_1A_\ell)^2=0$. Thus (10.2) directly satisfies every condition in (1.3). The joint law (1.4) has a persistent label $L\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$, and conditional on $L=\ell$ its visible law is $R^{a_\ell}$. All expectations involving $L$ below are under this one joint law, denoted $J^{(N)}$.
+
+The component insertion ratios, including $n=1$ and open endpoints, are exactly (3.4), and their linear inequalities survive the mixture. Each component whole-word marginal and each actual component block conditional has all nonnegative cut ranks at most two. Thus $\mathscr F_{N,n}^{0,0}$ is nonempty for $N\ge2$, and the component conditional is feasible in $\mathscr F_{N,t}^{a,b}$, including endpoint blocks and singleton completion sets. No conversion from real rank to a stationary realization is being made; (10.2) already supplies the actual nonnegative realization and all seams.
+
+The $z_\ell$ are distinct because $a/(1-a)^2$ is strictly increasing on $(0,1)$. For $0\le j\le k-1$ the legal word
+
+$$
+w_j=(10)^j0^{m-2j}\in B_m
+\tag{10.8}
+$$
+
+has $j$ ones, also at $j=k-1$ when the final zero string is empty. The matrix with rows $j$ and columns $\ell$ given by $v_\ell(w_j)=z_\ell^j/Z_\ell$ has determinant
+
+$$
+\left(\prod_{\ell=1}^kZ_\ell^{-1}\right)
+\prod_{\ell<h}(z_h-z_\ell)\ne0.
+\tag{10.9}
+$$
+
+Hence the vectors $v_\ell$ are linearly independent. The coefficient $b_\ell$ is the stationary probability, under component $\ell$, that the two endpoints of a segment of $m+1$ transitions are both zero. It is positive, for example because the all-zero path has positive probability. Therefore $G$ has rank $k$ and $\gamma=\lambda_k(G)>0$.
+
+Fix any interior length-$m$ interval $C=[c,d]$ and put
+
+$$
+\mathcal H=\sigma(W_{C^c}),\qquad
+\theta_\ell=J^{(N)}(L=\ell\mid\mathcal H),\qquad
+E=\{W_{c-1}=W_{d+1}=0\}\in\mathcal H.
+\tag{10.10}
+$$
+
+These are the posterior weights given the entire finite complement, not just its adjacent bits. On $E$, Proposition 3.3 gives the exact identity
+
+$$
+\mu_n(W_C=\cdot\mid\mathcal H)=\sum_{\ell=1}^k\theta_\ell v_\ell
+=\mathbb E_{J^{(N)}}[v_L\mid\mathcal H].
+\tag{10.11}
+$$
+
+Stationarity and the actual component transition law give
+
+$$
+J^{(N)}(L=\ell,E)=w_\ell b_\ell.
+\tag{10.12}
+$$
+
+In particular these weights are not replaced by the prior $w_\ell$ or normalized by $J^{(N)}(E)$.
+
+The complement contains a contiguous observed segment of length $s\ge(n-m)/2$. Lemma 4.3 applies under every component because $s\Delta\ge4$, including equality. Its nearest-mean classifier uses only that segment and has error at most
+
+$$
+\varepsilon_n=2\exp\left(-\frac{(n-m)\Delta^2}{64}\right).
+\tag{10.13}
+$$
+
+Given $\mathcal H$, the least conditional error of a label guess is $1-\max_\ell\theta_\ell$. A guess using the whole complement can use this segment classifier, so
+
+$$
+\mathbb E_{J^{(N)}}(1-\max_\ell\theta_\ell)\le\varepsilon_n.
+\tag{10.14}
+$$
+
+The bound is uniform in the position of $C$ for this fixed law. The constants depend on its separated means; there is no parameter-uniform rate.
+
+Let $V=v_L$ as a random column vector, and put
+
+$$
+G_{n,C}=\bigl(S_C^{0,0}(\mu_n)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}S_C^{0,0}(\mu_n).
+$$
+
+Equations (9.2), (10.11) and (10.12), with the original complement masses in (9.2), yield
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+G&=\mathbb E_{J^{(N)}}[\mathbf1_EVV^{\mathsf T}],\\
+G_{n,C}&=\mathbb E_{J^{(N)}}\left[\mathbf1_E
+\mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal H]\mathbb E[V\mid\mathcal H]^{\mathsf T}\right],\\
+G-G_{n,C}&=\mathbb E_{J^{(N)}}[\mathbf1_E\operatorname{Cov}(V\mid\mathcal H)]\succeq0.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{10.15}
+$$
+
+At a given complement choose an index $h$ of largest $\theta_h$. Conditional means minimize squared Euclidean error. Since probability vectors have squared Euclidean distance at most two,
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Cov}(V\mid\mathcal H)
+&\le\sum_\ell\theta_\ell\|v_\ell-v_h\|_2^2
+\le2(1-\theta_h),\\
+\|G-G_{n,C}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+&\le\operatorname{tr}(G-G_{n,C})
+\le2\varepsilon_n.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{10.16}
+$$
+
+For the second line, positivity in (10.15) bounds the operator norm by the trace, and dropping $\mathbf1_E$ enlarges a nonnegative expectation. The eigenvalue variational principle gives
+
+$$
+\lambda_k(G_{n,C})\ge\gamma-2\varepsilon_n,\qquad
+\operatorname{tail}_{N^2}(S_C^{0,0}(\mu_n))
+\ge[\gamma-2\varepsilon_n]_+,
+\tag{10.17}
+$$
+
+because $k=N^2+1$. Choose $\lfloor(n-2)/m\rfloor$ consecutive disjoint length-$m$ intervals in $[2,n-1]$. Apply Theorem 9.2, retaining only their $00$ types. Equations (10.13) and (10.17) prove (10.5), and division by $n$ gives (10.6). The contexts of neighboring chosen blocks may overlap; Theorem 9.2 requires only disjoint site sets.
+
+For (10.7), fix $t$ and a block $C_j$ of that length. Under the same $J^{(N)}$ define $\theta_{\ell,j}=J^{(N)}(L=\ell\mid W_{C_j^c})$. Its actual conditional is the mixture of its actual component conditionals with these weights, as in (3.5). Lemma 4.2, with comparison rank $N\ge2$, gives
+
+$$
+\delta_{N,t}^{a_j,b_j}\bigl(\mu_n(W_{C_j}=\cdot\mid W_{C_j^c})\bigr)
+\le t(1-\max_\ell\theta_{\ell,j}).
+\tag{10.18}
+$$
+
+Indeed, its proof compares with a largest-weight feasible rank-two component, using convexity in the first argument of $\mathcal D_K$ and the bound $t$ on that discrepancy. It does not require an interior block. A complement segment has length at least $(n-t)/2$, so the same application of Lemma 4.3 and Bayes comparison gives
+
+$$
+\mathbb E_{J^{(N)}}(1-\max_\ell\theta_{\ell,j})
+\le2\exp\left(-\frac{(n-t)\Delta^2}{64}\right).
+\tag{10.19}
+$$
+
+There are at most $n/t$ disjoint blocks, proving (10.7). At an endpoint the component law in (10.18) is its true conditional; (3.6) is not used there. Thus the statement retains open endpoints, all original legal words, the same common matrices at every length and the entire complement in every predictor. $\square$
+
+## 11. The actual-optimizer consumer and its spectral premise
+
+**Corollary 11.1 (Shared-context sufficient inequality on the original optimizer).** For fixed $N\ge1$, $n\ge1$ and disjoint nonempty interior intervals $C_j$, define
+
+$$
+\Lambda_{N,n}(\pi_n;\{C_j\})=
+\sum_jc_{|C_j|}\sum_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}
+\operatorname{tail}_{N^2}\bigl(S_{C_j}^{a,b}(\pi_n)\bigr).
+\tag{11.1}
+$$
+
+If
+
+$$
+\Lambda_{N,n}(\pi_n;\{C_j\})>
+\tau=2(3-2\sqrt2)-\frac1{24},
+\tag{11.2}
+$$
+
+then $C_N<c_\star$ on the entire original $\Theta_N$ of (1.3).
+
+Proof. The fixed-producer geometric entropy-tail bound of [Stripping, Theorems 3.1, 5.1 and 6.5][SC-S], together with the same-law whole-half-line comparison of [Entropy erasure, Theorem 3.1][SC-H], supplies $A_{P_\theta}<\infty$ for every fixed finite $\theta\in\Theta_N$. Specifically, the comparison bounds each $e_L(j),e_R(j)$ by half the geometrically decreasing $R_j$ of Stripping; their square roots are summable. The zero-tail case has the same conclusion. This reuse needs no band, identifiability, irreducibility, aperiodicity or uniformity over $\Theta_N$.
+
+Suppose a single $\theta\in\Theta_N$ attained $d(P_\theta)=c_\star$. Its band follows from [Universal, Theorem 3.1][U]. The just cited root sum and [Attainment, Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 9.1][SC-A] give strong zero for that same actual law and its original full-exterior predictors. [Guarded, Corollary 6.4][SC-G] therefore applies to that $J_\theta/P_\theta$ and gives
+
+$$
+\mathcal R_{N,n}\le(n+2)c_\star-\kappa_n-\frac1{24}\le\tau.
+\tag{11.3}
+$$
+
+Its guarded kernels are the actual conditional laws supplied by [Guarded, Theorem 6.2][SC-G], not laws inferred from a rank converse. Theorem 9.2 with $p=\pi_n$ gives $\mathcal R_{N,n}\ge\Lambda_{N,n}(\pi_n;\{C_j\})$, contradicting (11.2). Thus no $\theta\in\Theta_N$ attains $c_\star$. The fixed-dimension maximum theorem [Universal, Theorem 6.2][U] then makes the gap strict: $C_N=\max_{\theta\in\Theta_N}d(P_\theta)<c_\star$. All implications apply to the entire original domain, including stationary mixtures, structural zeros, zero stationary masses, reducibility, periodicity and redundant presentations. $\square$
+
+**Proposition 11.2 (Scope of the compatibility separation).** For every $N\ge2$, Theorem 10.1 disproves the implication from vanishing sums of independently minimized fixed-block discrepancies, for every fixed block length, to $\mathscr R_{N,n}(\mu_n)=o(n)$, even among marginals of one actual stationary finite producer with the band at every length. The law in that theorem satisfies
+
+$$
+A_{P^{(N)}}\le2,\qquad d(P^{(N)})\le\frac17<c_\star,
+\qquad\neg\mathsf Z_\Delta(P^{(N)}).
+\tag{11.4}
+$$
+
+It supplies no instance of (11.2). A sufficient unresolved optimizer inequality for each intended $N$ is precisely
+
+$$
+\exists n,\ \exists\{C_j\}\text{ disjoint interior intervals}:\quad
+\sum_j\frac{6^{-4|C_j|}}{2|C_j|}
+\sum_{a,b}\operatorname{tail}_{N^2}\bigl(S_{C_j}^{a,b}(\pi_n)\bigr)>\tau.
+\tag{11.5}
+$$
+
+Proof. The two limits (10.6)–(10.7) contradict that implication for the same law $P^{(N)}$. Proposition 6.3 applies to its finite persistent mixture, proving (11.4) with the original entire-exterior density. Its exhibited hidden dimension is $2(N^2+1)$, whereas the comparison rank is $N$; it is not an $N$-state attainer. Every matrix in (11.5) instead uses the conditionals and weights of the actual full optimizer $\pi_n$. Theorems 9.2 and 10.1 establish neither a positive lower bound for those tails nor a coupling that transfers (10.17) to them. The implication from (11.5) is Corollary 11.1, whose strict spectral premise remains additional. In particular, no all-$N$ strict-gap conclusion or finite attainer follows from this comparison construction. $\square$
+
+## 12. Mathematical citations for the shared-context criterion
+
+[Guarded][SC-G], *FIB harmonic-edge load: guarded replacement, attainment and conditional-rank obstruction*, Lemma 8.1 supplies the constant $c_m$ on the hard legal completion graph, including singleton and forcing cases. Definition 6.3 supplies the all-cut nonnegative-rank family; Theorem 6.2 and Corollary 6.4 supply the actual-law guarded conditional and its budget. Propositions 3.2–3.3 and Lemmas 4.2–4.3 of the present volume supply the stationary mixture, actual conditional weights, independent-fit bound and classifier; Theorem 5.1 is its rank-two global/local separation. These remain the suppliers for Theorems 9.2 and 10.1.
+
+[Intrinsic][SC-I], *FIB harmonic-edge load: intrinsic-null kernels, dual residuals and presentation obstruction*, §2 supplies the finite-realization context-rank mechanism. [Whitebox][SC-W], *FIB atom machine-learning whitebox*, Theorem 43.5 supplies the weighted projection/spectral-tail mechanism in a different readout problem. [Product-upper and phase-cut rank][SC-P], §23 concerns upper Schmidt-tail bounds for coherent square-root probability amplitudes. Those matrices and upper bounds are different from the weighted conditional probability tables and lower Brier-discrepancy bound in (9.2)–(9.4).
+
+[Dawid–Lauritzen–Parry][SC-DLP], *Proper local scoring rules on discrete sample spaces*, §4.2, Example 4.4 and (14), gives the conditional Brier/ratio-matching background. Its everywhere-positive product-space hypotheses are not a substitute for the hard no11 graph coercivity cited above. [Balle–Panangaden–Precup][SC-BPP], *A Canonical Form for Weighted Automata and Applications to Approximate Minimization*, §2.2, treats real weighted realizations and Hankel rank factorization. No positive stationary realization converse is used here. [Eckart–Young][SC-EY], *The Approximation of One Matrix by Another of Lower Rank*, is the classical matrix approximation reference; the full lower-bound argument needed here is (9.9). The discrepancy application and its common-law comparison in §§9–11 are a synthesis of these tools, without a literature-priority assertion.
+
+[Stripping][SC-S], *Equivalent-mass stripping and exponential terminal information*, Theorems 3.1, 5.1 and 6.5, gives fixed-producer geometric entropy tails on the original full domain. [Entropy erasure][SC-H], *Entropy gaps and actual erased-center influence*, Theorem 3.1, compares those tails with both actual complete-half-line erasure defects. [Attainment][SC-A], *Attainment, strong-zero equivalence and finite-optimizer comparison*, Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 9.1, supplies the attainment-to-strong-zero bridge under the resulting root sum. The constants remain law-dependent, and the common-law spectral premise (11.5) is separate from every one of these suppliers.

+## 11. Forward-only quotient laws and a legal $\Theta_4$ witness

+**Proposition 11.1 (forward-only quotient-law reduction).** Fix a finite positive stationary irreducible component $C$, with positive stationary vector $\lambda$, labeled matrices $M_0,M_1$, and visible law $P_C$. Let $\pi:C\to S$ be surjective and suppose only the forward labeled strong lumpability identities (3.2). Define
+
+$$
+\bar\lambda_u=\sum_{s:\pi(s)=u}\lambda_s,
+\qquad
+\sum_{t:\pi(t)=v}M_x(s,t)=\bar M_x(u,v)
+\quad (\pi(s)=u).
+$$
+
+Then $\bar A=\bar M_0+\bar M_1$ is stochastic, $\bar\lambda\bar A=\bar\lambda$, and $\bar\lambda_u>0$. The quotient producer $\bar\theta=(\bar\lambda,\bar M_0,\bar M_1)$ is in the same legal class $\Theta_{|S|}$, and its visible law equals $P_C$. Its canonical stationary reverse is the family
+
+$$
+R_x(u,v)=
+\frac{\bar\lambda_v\,\bar M_x(v,u)}{\bar\lambda_u}.
+\tag{11.1}
+$$
+
+Thus $R_0+R_1$ is stochastic and $\bar\lambda_uR_x(u,v)=\bar\lambda_v\bar M_x(v,u)$. If the forward matrices $\bar M_x$ and the canonical reverse matrices $R_x$ satisfy the two all-feasible-word diameter hypotheses (3.7), with constants $m_\pm,\rho_\pm$, then the original visible law $P_C$ satisfies exactly the bounds (6.1)--(6.3), with those constants. If every positive stationary component of an original producer has such a forward quotient and such constants, the mixture conclusion (7.1)--(7.3) applies.
+
+**Proof.** Summing (3.2) over $v$ and $x$ gives the row sums of $\bar A$. Summing the stationary flux over the fibers gives $\bar\lambda\bar A=\bar\lambda$. For a quotient-state cylinder, repeated use of (3.2) gives
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+&J_C(Q_a=u_a,\ldots,Q_{b+1}=u_{b+1},X_a=x_a,\ldots,X_b=x_b)\\
+&\qquad=\bar\lambda_{u_a}\prod_{i=a}^{b}\bar M_{x_i}(u_i,u_{i+1}),
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{11.2}
+$$
+
+where $Q_i=\pi(H_i)$. Summing (11.2) over the quotient endpoints proves equality of all visible cylinders with the quotient producer. In particular,
+
+$$
+\bar\lambda\bar M_1^2\mathbf 1
+ =P_C(X_0=X_1=1)=0,
+$$
+
+so the quotient remains in $\Theta_{|S|}$. Irreducibility passes to the quotient: a positive hidden $A$-path between two fibers maps to a positive quotient path. Formula (11.1) is well-defined because every $\bar\lambda_u$ is positive; stationarity gives
+
+$$
+\sum_{v,x}R_x(u,v)
+ =\frac{1}{\bar\lambda_u}\sum_v\bar\lambda_v\bar A(v,u)=1.
+$$

+The identity quotient of $\bar\theta$ satisfies both labeled identities, with its reverse matrices equal to $R_x$. +## 12. Posterior-variance-weighted block contraction
+
+**Lemma 12.1 (conditional variance-weighted block contraction).** Use the setup of Lemma 5.1: $U$ is binary, $Z,Z'$ are finite, $V$ is conditioning data, $W$ ranges over a finite family of words, and the matrices $B_w$ satisfy (5.1) and $\sum_wB_w\mathbf1=\mathbf1$. For almost every $V=v$, put
+
+$$
+p_v(w)=\mathbb P(W=w\mid V=v),\qquad
+\Delta_w(v)=\mathcal D(U;Z\mid V=v,W=w)\quad(p_v(w)>0),
+\qquad
+\Delta(v)=\sum_{w:p_v(w)>0} p_v(w)\Delta_w(v).
+\tag{12.1}
+$$
+
+Assume $0\le\delta(B_w)\le1$ for every $w$ with $p_v(w)>0$, and that, for some $0\le\kappa<1$,
+
+$$
+\sum_{w:p_v(w)>0} p_v(w)\,\delta(B_w)\,\Delta_w(v)
+\le \kappa\,\Delta(v)
+\tag{12.2}
+$$
+
+for almost every $v$ with $\Delta(v)>0$. All sums involving $\Delta_w(v)$ range over positive-probability words; zero-probability conditional versions are omitted. No diameter or conditional variance is assigned to a null word; in particular, the zero matrix remains excluded as in Definition 3.4. Fibers with $\Delta(v)=0$ are vacuous: every $\Delta_w(v)$ with positive $p_v(w)$ is then zero. Under these assumptions,
+
+$$
+\mathcal D(U;Z'\mid V,W)
+\le
+\kappa\bigl[\mathcal D(U;Z\mid V)-\mathcal D(U;W\mid V)\bigr]
+\le
+\kappa\,\mathcal D(U;Z\mid V).
+\tag{12.3}
+$$
+
+The hypothesis (12.2) is fiberwise in the posterior variances. It is not a stationary word average.
+
+**Proof.** Fix a $V=v$ fiber and a word $w$ of positive conditional probability. The conditional kernel in (5.4) has row diameter $\delta(B_w)$, so the conditional form of Lemma 4.3, applied on this $(v,w)$-fiber, gives
+
+$$
+\mathcal D(U;Z'\mid V=v,W=w)
+\le \delta(B_w)\Delta_w(v).
+$$
+
+Multiply by $p_v(w)$, sum over $w$, and use (12.2). Integrating over $v$ gives
+
+$$
+\mathcal D(U;Z'\mid V,W)\le\kappa\,\mathcal D(U;Z\mid V,W).
+$$
+
+The variance identity (5.5) rewrites the last factor as
+$\mathcal D(U;Z\mid V)-\mathcal D(U;W\mid V)$, and dropping the nonnegative term $\mathcal D(U;W\mid V)$ gives (12.3). No comparison of the reweighted priors in (5.3) is used. $\square$
+
+**Corollary 12.2 (good/bad sufficient condition).** In the setup of Lemma 12.1, let the word family be split into good and bad words, $G\sqcup H$. Suppose $0\le\rho,\eta\le1$,
+
+$$
+\delta(B_w)\le\rho\quad(w\in G,\ p_v(w)>0),
+\qquad
+\sum_{w\in H,\ p_v(w)>0}p_v(w)\Delta_w(v)\le\eta\,\Delta(v)
+\tag{12.4}
+$$
+
+for almost every $v$. Then (12.2) holds with
+
+$$
+\kappa=\rho+(1-\rho)\eta.
+\tag{12.5}
+$$
+
+In particular, if $\rho+(1-\rho)\eta<1$, Lemma 12.1 gives strict contraction.
+
+**Proof.** Since every diameter is at most one,
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\sum_{w:p_v(w)>0}p_v(w)\delta(B_w)\Delta_w(v)
+&\le \rho\sum_{w\in G,\ p_v(w)>0}p_v(w)\Delta_w(v)
+   +\sum_{w\in H,\ p_v(w)>0}p_v(w)\Delta_w(v)\\
+&=\rho\left(\Delta(v)-\sum_{w\in H,\ p_v(w)>0}p_v(w)\Delta_w(v)\right)
+  +\sum_{w\in H,\ p_v(w)>0}p_v(w)\Delta_w(v)\\
+&\le \rho\Delta(v)+(1-\rho)\eta\Delta(v).
+\end{aligned}
+$$

+**Proposition 13.1 (an actual periodic producer in the posterior band).** Order the states as
+

+A=(0,0),\quad B=(0,1),\quad C=(1,0),\quad D=(1,1),
+$$
+
+where $H_i=(S_i,X_{i-1})$ records a phase and the previous emitted bit. Set
+
+$$
+M_0=\begin{pmatrix}
+0&0&3/4&0\\
+0&0&1&0\\
+2/3&0&0&0\\
+1&0&0&0
+\end{pmatrix},\qquad
+M_1=\begin{pmatrix}
+0&0&0&1/4\\
+0&0&0&0\\
+0&1/3&0&0\\
+0&0&0&0
+\end{pmatrix},\qquad
+\lambda=\frac1{22}(8,3,9,2).
+\tag{13.1}
+$$
+
+This is a stationary legal irreducible producer in $\Theta_4$, of period exactly two. Either infinite observed half-line determines $S_0$ almost surely. Its full-exterior posterior is
+
+$$
+q_0=\begin{cases}
+1/3,&X_{-1}=X_1=0,\ S_0=0,\\
+2/5,&X_{-1}=X_1=0,\ S_0=1,\\
+0,&\{X_{-1}=X_1=0\}^{c}.
+\end{cases}
+\tag{13.2}
+$$
+
+In particular its visible law satisfies the original band $\mathsf B(P)$.

+
+$$
+\lambda A=\frac1{22}(9\cdot2/3+2,\ 9/3,\ 8\cdot3/4+3,\ 8/4)
+=\frac1{22}(8,3,9,2).
+$$
+
+Also $M_1^2=0$. The cycle $A\to D\to A$ and the paths $A\to C\to B\to C\to A$ connect all states. Every transition changes phase, so every return length is even; the two-step return at $A$ makes the period exactly two. These are properties of the original labeled edge law (2.2).
+
+Write $a_0=1/4$, $a_1=1/3$, and $t_s=1-a_s$. Given phase $s$ and previous bit zero, the next emitted bit is one with probability $a_s$; after a one the next bit is zero with probability one. Every transition satisfies $S_{i+1}=1-S_i$ and gives the endpoint previous bit $X_i$. The phase-conditioned stationary distributions of $H_i$ are $(8,3)/11$ on $\{A,B\}$ and $(9,2)/11$ on $\{C,D\}$. The two-step transition matrices on these classes are, respectively,
+
+$$
+\begin{pmatrix}3/4&1/4\\2/3&1/3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
+\begin{pmatrix}5/6&1/6\\3/4&1/4\end{pmatrix}.
+$$
+
+Both have strictly positive entries. The classical finite-chain occupation theorem, applied to these two-step chains, yields the emitted-one frequencies
+
+$$
+r_0=\mathbb P(X_i=1\mid S_i=0)=\frac8{11}\frac14=\frac2{11},
+\qquad
+r_1=\mathbb P(X_i=1\mid S_i=1)=\frac9{11}\frac13=\frac3{11}.
+\tag{13.3}
+$$
+
+For example, conditional on $S_0=s$, the empirical averages of $X_{2n}$ and $X_{2n-1}$, $1\le n\le k$, converge as $k\to\infty$ to $r_s$ and $r_{1-s}$. One can obtain this directly from the second coordinate of $H_{2n+1}$ and $H_{2n}$, respectively. For the left half-line the averages of $X_{-2n}$ and $X_{-(2n-1)}$ have the same two limits, by the occupation theorem for the stationary reversed two-step chains. Since $r_0\ne r_1$, either half-line determines $S_0$. This is an infinite-frequency assertion: every finite legal word has positive probability under each possible phase at its start, by starting with previous bit zero, so no such finite word identifies the phase.

+
+$$
+X_0=0:\ t_st_{1-s}=\frac12,
+\qquad
+X_0=1:\ a_s\cdot1.
+$$

+\tag{17.7}

Every return length is divisible by $m$, since every edge advances phase. The all-zero path from $(s,0)$ returns to it in exactly $m$ steps with positive probability. Thus the hidden period is exactly $m$, even when the parameter profile has a smaller period. Its stationary phase marginal is uniform. The $m$-step chain on the two previous-bit states at a fixed phase is irreducible and aperiodic; irreducibility also follows by padding the zero paths just described with full zero cycles.

+$$

+\begin{aligned}

+ &=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{k=2}^{N+1}
+       \mathbf1_{\{x_{t_{i,j,k}^{\pm}-1}=0\}},\\

+\tag{17.8}

+$$

+q=\mathbb E_P[X_0\mid\mathcal E_0],\quad I=[1/4,1/2].
+\tag{55.1}
+$$
+
+直接使用 [Universal 卷][U] 定理 2.2、3.1 的供应
+
+$$
+c_\star-d(P)\ge\Delta(P):=
+\mathbb E_P[\mathbf1_{F_0}\operatorname{dist}(q,I)^2],
+\qquad d(P)=c_\star\Longrightarrow q\in I\text{ 于 }F_0\text{ 几乎处处}.
+\tag{55.2}
+$$
+
+达到者的完整合法支撑也由同一定理供应。本节的事件标记不是从有限隐藏维数推出的。第 9–15 节已处理循环几何等待及其旋转商；下面的新增对象是实际标记的拆分相容性，以及允许零支撑的任意有限均值循环独立间隔。
+
+**假设 55.2（实际双侧可观察标记）。** $J$ 是一个两侧平稳联合律，其可见边缘为同一个平稳合法律 $P$。占据位在两个方向均无界，$\iota=P(X_0=1)>0$；每个占据位 $t$ 带标记 $C_t$，值域为有限非空集 $E$。存在固定可测函数 $L,R$，使对每个确定整数 $t$，在 $\{X_t=1\}$ 上
+
+$$
+C_t=L((X_{t-j})_{j\ge0})=R((X_{t+j})_{j\ge0})
+\quad J\text{-几乎处处}.
+\tag{55.3}
+$$
+
+令 $Q=J(\,\cdot\mid X_0=1)$，在此实际 Palm 律下按序列出占据位
+
+$$
+\cdots<S_{-1}<S_0=0<S_1<\cdots,\quad
+G_k=S_{k+1}-S_k\ge2,\quad C_k^{\rm e}=C_{S_k}.
+\tag{55.4}
+$$
+
+置 $\nu_a=Q(C_0^{\rm e}=a)>0$，并定义实际条件质量
+
+$$
+f_a(g)=Q(G_0=g\mid C_0^{\rm e}=a),\quad
+p_a(l,r)=Q(G_0=l,G_1=r\mid C_0^{\rm e}=a).
+\tag{55.5}
+$$
+
+每个 $f_a$ 均有有限均值。对每个 $g\ge2$ 给定映射 $T_g:E\to E$，实际连续事件满足
+
+$$
+C_{k+1}^{\rm e}=T_{G_k}(C_k^{\rm e})\quad(k\in\mathbb Z)
+\quad Q\text{-几乎处处}.
+\tag{55.6}
+$$
+
+相应的一步标记矩阵
+
+$$
+K(a,b)=\sum_{g\ge2}f_a(g)\mathbf1_{\{T_g(a)=b\}}
+\tag{55.7}
+$$
+
+不可约。这里没有假定标记序列为 Markov 链，也没有假定给定当前标记后下个间隔独立于事件过去。第 57 节的全分类另要求每个 $a\in E,g\ge2$ 均有 $f_a(g)>0$；第 56 节的实际质量恒等式允许零值。
+
+## 56. 实际外部胞元的拆分缺陷
+
+**定理 56.1（无独立性假设的拆分证书）。** 在假设 55.2 下，对 $a,b\in E$ 及 $l,r\ge2$ 置
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+u_{a,b,l,r}&=f_a(l+r)\mathbf1_{\{b=T_{l+r}(a)\}},\\
+v_{a,b,l,r}&=p_a(l,r)\mathbf1_{\{b=T_r(T_l(a))\}},\\
+D(u,v)&=\frac{(u-3v)_+^2}{16(u+v)}+
+\frac{(v-u)_+^2}{4(u+v)},\qquad D(0,0)=0.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{56.1}
+$$
+
+这里 $u_{a,b,l,r}$ 的首字母为 $u$，与平稳权重 $\nu_a$ 不同。则
+
+$$
+c_\star-d(P)\ge\Delta(P)\ge
+\iota\sum_a\nu_a\sum_{l,r\ge2}\sum_b
+D(u_{a,b,l,r},v_{a,b,l,r}).
+\tag{56.2}
+$$
+
+特别地，若 $T_{l+r}(a)\ne T_r(T_l(a))$，则
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+P(F_0\cap\{q=0\})&\ge\iota\nu_a f_a(l+r),\\
+P(F_0\cap\{q=1\})&\ge\iota\nu_a p_a(l,r),\\
+c_\star-d(P)&\ge\iota\nu_a\left(\frac{f_a(l+r)}{16}+
+\frac{p_a(l,r)}4\right).
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{56.3}
+$$
+
+第一项的严格正性只需要该实际一间隔边缘为正，不需要两间隔概率为正或有乘积形式。
+
+**证明。** 先在同一实际联合律内核对 Palm 权重：$Q$ 对移至下个占据位并重新编号的事件移位不变，$\nu K=\nu$，且
+
+$$
+1=\iota\sum_a\nu_a\sum_{g\ge2}g f_a(g).
+\tag{56.4}
+$$
+
+可在选择任何最近锚之前，取一个 $J$ 满测集，使（55.3）对其上所有实际占据位同时成立。
+
+记联合配置的整数移位为 $\vartheta$，$Q$ 上的事件移位为 $\mathsf S\omega=\vartheta^{G_0}\omega$。对以零为占据锚的任意可测事件 $A$，平稳性给出
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\iota Q(\mathsf S^{-1}A)
+&=\sum_{g\ge2}J(X_0=1,G_0=g,\vartheta^g\omega\in A)\\
+&=\sum_{g\ge2}J(X_{-g}=1,X_{-g+1}=\cdots=X_{-1}=0,X_0=1,\omega\in A)\\
+&=\iota Q(A).
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{56.5}
+$$
+
+最后的事件按零之前的最近占据位分割 $\{X_0=1\}\cap A$。于是事件移位不变，取下一标记的边缘并用（55.6）得到 $\nu K=\nu$。
+
+每个原整数位置有唯一的前一占据位，包含该位置自身可能为占据位的情形。按此锚的距离 $s\ge0$ 分割原位置零，再平移到该锚，有
+
+$$
+1=\sum_{s\ge0}J(X_{-s}=1,\text{其下个占据位}>0)
+=\iota\sum_{s\ge0}Q(G_0>s)=\iota\mathbb E_QG_0.
+\tag{56.6}
+$$
+
+此处 $s=0$ 项解释为 $X_0=1$，其下个事件严格在零之后。非负尾和及（55.5）给（56.4）。更一般地，对任意可见可测事件 $A$，同一分割给出
+
+$$
+P(A)=\iota\mathbb E_Q\sum_{s=0}^{G_0-1}
+\mathbf1_A(\vartheta^sX).
+\tag{56.7}
+$$
+
+各项对应 $s$ 之前的实际占据锚；先对非负指标使用可数可加性即可，无须独立性。最后对（55.3）的零例外集按全部确定整数取并，同样平移（55.6）的 Palm 零例外，再交上双向无界事件，得到所需满测集。后续随机锚仅从已覆盖的整数中选择，不产生新的条件独立性。
+
+定义 $A(a,b;l,r)$：零左边最近的占据位为 $-l$，右边最近的占据位为 $r$，在 $-l$ 用过去解码器得到 $a$，在 $r$ 用未来解码器得到 $b$。最近锚由非零坐标决定；左解码器只看 $j\le-l$，右解码器只看 $j\ge r$。故 $A(a,b;l,r)\in\mathcal E_0$。$l,r\ge2$ 恰保证两个邻位为零；在合法外部上，中心的零、一两种补全在 no11 意义下都合法。因此这些胞元不删改原自由事件 $F_0$。由上述可数交，全部解码恒等式先在同一满测集成立；双向无界性使这些可数胞元在零集之外分割整个 $F_0$。
+
+在 $A\cap\{X_0=0\}$ 上，两锚是连续事件，其端点标记必为 $a,T_{l+r}(a)$。由确定位置 $-l$ 的平稳性及实际 Palm 边缘，
+
+$$
+P(A(a,b;l,r),X_0=0)=\iota\nu_a u_{a,b,l,r}.
+\tag{56.8}
+$$
+
+在 $A\cap\{X_0=1\}$ 上，连续事件恰为 $-l,0,r$，端点标记为 $a,T_r(T_l(a))$。此时使用的是同一 Palm 律内的实际两间隔质量，而非两个边缘的乘积：
+
+$$
+P(A(a,b;l,r),X_0=1)=\iota\nu_a v_{a,b,l,r}.
+\tag{56.9}
+$$
+
+反过来，每个上述实际一间隔或两间隔事件都给出相应胞元；其另一侧解码值由（55.3）自动正确，所以没有额外尾条件因子。两式均为同一个 $J$ 内的事件质量恒等式，左侧只涉及可见变量，因而也是 $P$ 的恒等式。
+
+若 $u+v>0$，条件期望定义给 $\mathbb E_P[q\mid A]=v/(u+v)$。对凸函数 $z\mapsto\operatorname{dist}(z,I)^2$ 用条件 Jensen，得到
+
+$$
+\mathbb E_P[\mathbf1_A\operatorname{dist}(q,I)^2]
+\ge\iota\nu_a(u+v)\operatorname{dist}\left(\frac v{u+v},I\right)^2
+=\iota\nu_aD(u,v).
+\tag{56.10}
+$$
+
+当 $u=v=0$ 时两边贡献均为零。按分割求和即得（56.2）；实际胞元质量之和至多一，故该非负级数有界。这里复用 [Universal 卷][U] 推论 2.3 的 Jensen 机制，胞元允许依赖无限外部，但没有对单个无限配置取概率比。
+
+若两个端点不同，取 $b=T_{l+r}(a)$ 的胞元，其中心一质量为零，故 $q=0$ 于该胞元几乎处处，总质量为 $\iota\nu_a f_a(l+r)$。取 $b=T_r(T_l(a))$ 的另一个胞元，中心零质量为零，故 $q=1$，总质量为 $\iota\nu_a p_a(l,r)$。两胞元不交，平方带距离分别为 $1/16,1/4$，得到（56.3）。$\square$
+
+**推论 56.2（原带约束与明确的乘积特例）。** 在假设 55.2 下，若 $q\in I$ 于 $F_0$ 几乎处处，则对每个实际胞元都有
+
+$$
+u_{a,b,l,r}/3\le v_{a,b,l,r}\le u_{a,b,l,r}.
+\tag{56.11}
+$$
+
+等价地，$f_a(l+r)>0$ 当且仅当 $p_a(l,r)>0$；二者为正时端点标记相同，且
+
+$$
+f_a(l+r)/3\le p_a(l,r)\le f_a(l+r).
+\tag{56.12}
+$$
+
+若再明确假设完整事件历史下的 Markov 更新间隔规则
+
+$$
+\mathcal H_k=\sigma(C_j^{\rm e}:j\le k;\ G_j:j<k),\qquad
+Q(G_k=g\mid\mathcal H_k)=f_{C_k^{\rm e}}(g)
+\quad(k\in\mathbb Z,g\ge2),
+\tag{56.13}
+$$
+
+在此附加规则下，定理 56.1 中可作替换
+
+$$
+p_a(l,r)=f_a(l)f_{T_l(a)}(r).
+\tag{56.14}
+$$
+
+于是（56.2）给出完全由该同律的 $f_a,T_g,\iota,\nu$ 表示的定量证书，（56.12）成为相应的乘积带约束。对零支撑也成立；两侧质量都为零的胞元不对其端点映射施加方程。
+
+**证明。** 在每个胞元对 $1/4\le q\le1/2$ 积分，使用（56.8）–（56.9），恰得（56.11）。或由（56.2）每个非负项为零得到同一结论。若两端点不同，非零质量所在的两个胞元各有一侧为零，与（56.11）冲突，除非两种质量均为零；端点相同时（56.11）正是（56.12）。在（56.13）下先条件于 $\mathcal H_1$，再条件于 $C_0^{\rm e}=a,G_0=l$；实际输运给 $C_1^{\rm e}=T_l(a)$，塔性质遂给（56.14）。没有（56.13）时此步不能用 $f_{T_l(a)}(r)$ 替换条件质量，故基础定理始终保留 $p_a(l,r)$。$\square$
+
+## 57. 全正间隔下的完整有限空间时钟分类
+
+**定理 57.1（带约束迫使的变换分类）。** 在假设 55.2 下另设 $f_a(g)>0$ 对全部 $a\in E,g\ge2$ 成立。若原后验带成立，特别是若 $d(P)=c_\star$，则
+
+$$
+T_{l+r}=T_r\circ T_l\qquad(l,r\ge2).
+\tag{57.1}
+$$
+
+在这些全正边缘及不可约性条件下，有限变换族满足（57.1）当且仅当存在唯一的单循环置换 $U:E\to E$，使
+
+$$
+T_g=U^g\quad(g\ge2),\qquad U=T_3T_2^{-1}.
+\tag{57.2}
+$$
+
+因而可把 $E$ 标为 $\mathbb Z/|E|\mathbb Z$，使 $T_g(j)=j+g$。此等价只分类变换方程；它不把后验带、可观察性或达到性作为任意此形间隔核的结论。
+
+**证明。** 每个 $a,l,r$ 的一间隔质量 $\iota\nu_af_a(l+r)$ 严格为正。若端点不相容，（56.3）第一项使 $\Delta(P)>0$，违反带约束。故（57.1）逐状态成立。这一推论不使用（56.13）或（56.14）。
+
+交换 $l,r$ 得 $T_rT_l=T_lT_r$。对每个 $g\ge2$，非空像集 $I_g=T_g(E)$ 在所有 $T_h$ 下不变，因为 $T_hT_g=T_gT_h$。由（55.7），$I_g$ 对实际 $K$ 的所有转移封闭。有限不可约矩阵没有真非空封闭集：从其中任一点到外面一点的正概率路径必有首次离开步骤。故 $I_g=E$，所有 $T_g$ 均满射。仅到此时才由有限性推出它们是置换，未预先假设逆映射。
+
+令 $A=T_2,B=T_3$。它们交换，且
+
+$$
+B^2=T_6=A^3.
+\tag{57.3}
+$$
+
+定义 $U=BA^{-1}$。交换性及（57.3）给出 $U^2=B^2A^{-2}=A$、$U^3=B^3A^{-3}=B$。对 $n\ge4$，由（57.1）有 $T_n=T_{n-2}T_2$，包括 $n=4$ 的 $T_4=T_2^2$，因此归纳得到 $T_g=U^g$ 对全部 $g\ge2$ 成立。每个实际事件转移都留在一个 $U$ 轨道中；$K$ 不可约迫使仅有一个轨道，所以 $U$ 是单循环。任何符合幂式的 $U$ 必等于 $T_3T_2^{-1}$，故唯一。
+
+反之，单循环 $U$ 的幂显然满足（57.1）。全正 $f_a(g)$ 下，每个模 $|E|$ 的剩余类都含某个 $g\ge2$，所以从任一 $a$ 到任一 $b$ 的某个一步 $K(a,b)$ 项为正，因而不可约。这完成所述变换层面的分类。$\square$
+
+**约定 57.2（必要结构的边界）。** $T_g=U^g$ 以原空间距离 $g$ 推进；事件循环的 $T_g=V$ 则不论距离只推进一次。两者不同，后一形式在 $V\ne V^2$ 时违反（57.1）。若没有全正支撑，推论 56.2 仅约束实际非零胞元，不能将未出现的映射值扩成（57.1）。有限隐藏表示本身不供应假设 55.2 的双向解码和确定输运；即使（57.2）成立，也没有将任意这样的间隔核归约为最近邻位时钟生产者，更没有证明达到性或一般非达到性。
+
+## 58. 任意有限均值循环独立间隔的原位点二分
+
+**定义 58.1（循环分布词与实际平稳律）。** 固定有限 $m\ge1$，每个 $j\in\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$ 给定任意概率质量函数 $f_j$，支撑于 $\{2,3,\ldots\}$，均值有限。允许零质量、有限支撑及周期支撑。事件空间上规定同一个两侧概率律 $Q_f$：
+
+$$
+Q_f(C=c,G_k=g_k\ (-u\le k<v))
+=\frac1m\prod_{k=-u}^{v-1}f_{c+k}(g_k),\qquad u,v\ge0.
+\tag{58.1}
+$$
+
+相位指标模 $m$。记 $\bar\mu=m^{-1}\sum_j\sum_g g f_j(g)$。对事件移位
+$\mathsf S(C,(G_k))=(C+1,(G_{k+1}))$，采用 [更新闭包卷][CG-R] 定义 2.1 的整数悬挂，对应零数 $g_k^{\rm zero}=G_k-1$：
+
+$$
+\Omega_f=\{(C,G,s):0\le s<G_0\},\qquad
+\widehat Q_f(dC,dG,s)=\bar\mu^{-1}Q_f(dC,dG).
+\tag{58.2}
+$$
+
+原整数移位 $\mathsf V$ 在 $s<G_0-1$ 时使 $s$ 加一，在屋顶使事件基点变为 $\mathsf S(C,G)$ 并将 $s$ 置零。输出 $X_i=\mathbf1_{\{\mathsf V^i\text{ 的偏移为零}\}}$，其律为 $P_f$。在偏移零的事件赋予标记 $C$，以后每次事件标记加一。这规定了一份联合平稳标记律，不是对不同长度分别拟合的分布。
+
+**定理 58.2（真实稳定子、双侧解码与原风险）。** 定义分布词的整数周期群及旋转稳定子
+
+$$
+\mathcal P_f=\{h\in\mathbb Z:f_{j+h}=f_j\text{ 对所有 }j\}
+=d\mathbb Z,\qquad
+K_f=d\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z,\quad d\mid m.
+\tag{58.3}
+$$
+
+则 $P_f$ 是归一化两侧平稳 no11 律，两个方向均有无穷占据位，$\iota=1/\bar\mu$，其实际事件 Palm 律正是（58.1）。若 $d>1$，约化标记 $c_t=C_t\bmod d$ 在每个占据锚分别由左、右无限可见半线恢复，并有
+
+$$
+q=X_0\quad P_f\text{-几乎处处},\qquad d(P_f)=0.
+\tag{58.4}
+$$
+
+若 $d=1$，所有 $f_j=f$，$P_f$ 恰为零数分布 $w_n=f(n+1)$ 的平衡 iid 更新律。因而对定义 58.1 的整个明确类，一致有
+
+$$
+d(P_f)\le C_{\mathcal R}<c_\star,
+\tag{58.5}
+$$
+
+其中 $C_{\mathcal R}$ 完全复用 [更新闭包卷][CG-R] 定理 7.1。另有精确支撑判据
+
+$$
+P_f\text{ 的每个合法有限词均为正质量}
+\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+f_j(g)>0\text{ 对全部 }j\in\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z,\ g\ge2.
+\tag{58.6}
+$$
+
+**证明。** （58.1）的有限边缘相容，乘积概率扩张给事件律；对任意正负指标有限柱，$\mathsf S$ 只将起始相位和间隔指标同时前移，所以该律事件平稳。悬挂的总质量为 $\mathbb E_{Q_f}G_0/\bar\mu=1$。其可逆性由偏移减一、或在偏移零退回前一屋顶给出。对任意有界可测 $H$，每个屋顶上的相邻差相消，留下
+
+$$
+\int(H\circ\mathsf V-H)\,d\widehat Q_f
+=\bar\mu^{-1}\int[H(\mathsf S(C,G),0)-H(C,G,0)]\,dQ_f=0.
+\tag{58.7}
+$$
+
+这在所用事件基点上验证了供应悬挂的条件。距离至少二保证全部接缝合法；每个距离有限且基点序列双向无限，故位轨道上两个方向均有无穷事件。偏移零质量为 $1/\bar\mu$，条件化后正好是 $Q_f$。尤其原位点质量为
+
+$$
+J_f(X_0=1,C_0=c,G_k=g_k\ (-u\le k<v))
+=\frac1{m\bar\mu}\prod_{k=-u}^{v-1}f_{c+k}(g_k).
+\tag{58.8}
+$$
+
+没有把每事件概率误作每原位点概率。
+
+周期集对加减封闭且包含 $m\mathbb Z$，故存在唯一正因子 $d\mid m$ 使（58.3）成立。约化分布词无非零旋转稳定子。每个约化相位的 $m/d$ 个提升给出的全部正负间隔乘积完全相同，所以将（58.1）对提升求和得到
+
+$$
+Q_f(c_0=c,G_k=g_k\ (-u\le k<v))
+=\frac1d\prod_{k=-u}^{v-1}f_{c+k}(g_k),\qquad c\in\mathbb Z/d\mathbb Z.
+\tag{58.9}
+$$
+
+因此给定约化相位之后，完整两侧间隔仍独立；这一步不对不同的乘积律任意混合。
+
+现设 $d>1$。对于有限个互不相同的分布 $f_i,f_j$，各选一个整数 $h\ge2$ 使其单点概率不同，组成有限非空集合 $H$。用此集合定义
+
+$$
+V_c^+=(f_{c+r}(h):0\le r<d,h\in H),\qquad
+V_c^-=(f_{c-r-1}(h):0\le r<d,h\in H).
+\tag{58.10}
+$$
+
+两张有限表均单射：任一方向的全部坐标相等会使对应旋转上的每对分布相等，从而产生非零旋转稳定子。这里比较单点概率，不使用可能为零的前缀概率作除数。
+
+条件于真实约化相位 $c_0=c$，对固定 $r,h$，序列
+
+$$
+\mathbf1_{\{G_{kd+r}=h\}},\quad k\ge0,
+\qquad\text{及}\qquad
+\mathbf1_{\{G_{-kd-r-1}=h\}},\quad k\ge0
+\tag{58.11}
+$$
+
+分别独立同分布，均值为 $f_{c+r}(h)$ 及 $f_{c-r-1}(h)$。用第 11 节所用的有界 iid 强大数律，有限组频率分别收敛为 $V_c^+,V_c^-$；概率零、一也包含在内。两张表的逆像因此从未来间隔、过去间隔各自恢复同一个约化标记。每个间隔由相应无限可见半线中的连续占据位计算，故这确实是两个方向分别可见的解码器。对每个确定整数平移该 Palm 零例外，再对全部整数取交，得到先覆盖所有实际占据锚的共同满测集，采用定理 56.1 证明中的锚选择次序。
+
+仅从外部选择最近负、正占据锚 $L_0,R_0$。从 $L_0$ 只用过去解码器，从 $R_0$ 只用未来解码器，得到 $c_L,c_R$。在 $F_0$ 上，中心零时有一次事件推进，中心一时有两次，所以
+
+$$
+c_R-c_L=1+X_0\pmod d.
+\tag{58.12}
+$$
+
+当 $d>1$ 时模 $d$ 的一、二不同。定义一个总外部函数：仅当 $F_0$ 成立、两个占据列表无穷、所需频率极限存在且落在各自有限表中、并且 $c_R-c_L=2\pmod d$ 时取一，其余情形取零。整数命中位置由有限坐标计数确定；频率极限、表成员关系和有限逆表都可测。因此此函数为 $\mathcal E_0$ 可测。在共同满测集上由（58.12）等于 $X_0$；$F_0^c$ 上合法性强制中心零。它便是 $q$ 的版本，证明（58.4），恢复的是单个原位点而非任意被擦除块。
+
+若 $d=1$，（58.1）的完整正负间隔律就是 iid $f$；（58.2）逐项等于 [更新闭包卷][CG-R] 定义 2.1 的 $w_n=f(n+1)$ 悬挂。故是同一可见更新律，直接使用该卷定理 7.1 得（58.5）的常数分支。非常数分支风险零，而 $C_{\mathcal R}\ge0$，所以（58.5）覆盖整个所定义的类。这里没有重复证明更新非达到。
+
+若所有 $f_j(g)>0$，任意有限完整间隔串在任一相位均有正 Palm 质量。任意合法有限词可以在两端外面各补上占据锚，取足够长的首尾间隔，成为某个有限完整间隔串的子柱；全零词也可置于一个足够长的正质量间隔内部。由（58.8）及平移，每个原合法词均有正质量。反向，任取缺失的 $f_j(g)$，考察合法词 $1(0^{g-1}1)^m$。其实际柱概率为
+
+$$
+P_f([1(0^{g-1}1)^m])
+=\frac{\iota}{m}\sum_{c=0}^{m-1}\prod_{k=0}^{m-1}f_{c+k}(g)
+=\iota\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}f_j(g)=0.
+\tag{58.13}
+$$
+
+这证明（58.6），并表明双向无穷事件本身不供应完整支撑。$\square$
+
+**推论 58.3（拆分障碍的实际消费者）。** 若定义 58.1 的 $d>1$ 且全部间隔全正，则该实际约化标记满足假设 55.2，$T_g(c)=c+1$ 对全部 $g\ge2$ 成立，事件矩阵不可约。但 $T_{l+r}(c)=c+1$ 与 $T_rT_l(c)=c+2$ 不同，因此不可能满足原后验带。此处（58.4）给出更强的精确风险零；允许零支撑时仍由定理 58.2 直接保证，而不误用第 57 节的全正分类。
+
+**证明。** Palm 相位均匀，条件独立间隔的有限均值、两个半线解码及事件推进均已由定理 58.2 建立。一步事件更新是一个单循环，故不可约。两种端点对模 $d>1$ 不同，定理 56.1 即适用。$\square$

+## 59. 同一有限生产者实现循环相位型消费者
+
+**定理 59.1（有限实现与同律风险）。** 对定义 58.1 的每个相位 $j$，取一个有限非负次随机矩阵 $B_j$、概率行 $\alpha_j$，满足
+
+$$
+\rho(B_j)<1,\qquad b_j=\mathbf1-B_j\mathbf1\ge0,\qquad
+\alpha_jb_j=0,
+\qquad f_j(g)=\alpha_jB_j^{g-1}b_j\quad(g\ge2).
+\tag{59.1}
+$$
+
+令 $R_j=(I-B_j)^{-1}$，$N=\sum_j\dim B_j$，并在模 $m$ 的块上定义
+
+$$
+M_0=\operatorname{diag}(B_j),\qquad
+M_1(j,j+1)=b_j\alpha_{j+1},\qquad
+M_1(j,k)=0\ (k\ne j+1),
+\tag{59.2}
+$$
+
+$$
+z=\sum_j\alpha_jR_j\mathbf1,\qquad
+\lambda_j=\frac{\alpha_jR_j}{z}.
+\tag{59.3}
+$$
+
+则 $\theta=(\lambda,M_0,M_1)$ 属于定义 2.1 的原完整 $\Theta_N$，其同一平稳矩阵律在所有长度上恰为 $P_f$。因此该有限隐藏子类满足定理 58.2 的二分及（58.5），包含非几何、非 iid 更新的可见律。有限相位型吸收表示本身是经典工具；本定理将它用于这个非 iid 循环 Palm 消费者，而不把任意有限均值 $f_j$ 都声称为有限隐藏。
+
+**证明。** $R_j=\sum_{n\ge0}B_j^n\ge0$，且 $R_jb_j=\mathbf1$。因而
+
+$$
+\sum_{g\ge1}\alpha_jB_j^{g-1}b_j=1,\qquad
+\mathbb E_{f_j}G=\alpha_jR_j\mathbf1<\infty.
+\tag{59.4}
+$$
+
+第一式中距离一的项由 $\alpha_jb_j=0$ 消失。第二式由吸收尾概率 $\Pr(G>n)=\alpha_jB_j^n\mathbf1$ 的非负尾和得到。因此（59.1）确实提供定义 58.1 的概率质量函数，$z=m\bar\mu$。
+
+$\lambda$ 非负且归一化。（59.2）的每个块行总和为 $B_j\mathbf1+b_j=\mathbf1$。又
+
+$$
+\lambda_jb_j=1/z,\qquad
+\lambda_jB_j+\alpha_j/z=\lambda_j.
+\tag{59.5}
+$$
+
+第二式的 $\alpha_j/z$ 恰为从前一块经一边进入本块的平稳流，所以 $\lambda(M_0+M_1)=\lambda$。任何两条连续一边的乘积含有标量 $\alpha_{j+1}b_{j+1}=0$，故 $M_1^2=0$，包括 $m=1$。全部原 $\Theta_N$ 条件已验证，不要求内部块不可约，也不删除零平稳坐标。
+
+按 [Universal 卷][U] 命题 4.2，使用这些同一矩阵及同一 $\lambda$ 的两侧边发射联合律 $J_\theta$，每个可见柱均为 $\lambda M_w\mathbf1$。标记一个占据边为 $j$，当且仅当该边进入块 $j$。该事件的平稳质量是 $\lambda_{j-1}b_{j-1}=1/z$；其边后隐藏行重置为 $\alpha_j$。从此边后到下一个占据边，距离 $g$ 包含 $g-1$ 条零边，再有一条一边，其因子为 $\alpha_jB_j^{g-1}b_j=f_j(g)$，终点标记为 $j+1$。
+
+为核对完整两侧 Palm 律，给定 $-u\le k<v$ 的所有 $g_k$ 和中央标记 $j$。它们固定最左事件位置 $-\sum_{k=-u}^{-1}g_k$ 及其标记 $j-u$。从这个确定位置的平稳占据边开始，它只计一次通量 $1/z$；以后各段零边及秩一出口依次贡献 $f_{j+k}(g_k)$。求和内部隐藏路径，直接得到
+
+$$
+J_\theta(X_0=1,C_0=j,G_k=g_k\ (-u\le k<v))
+=\frac1z\prod_{k=-u}^{v-1}f_{j+k}(g_k).
+\tag{59.6}
+$$
+
+这个最左锚方法同时支付负指标，不使用反向重置假设。空乘积给 $J_\theta(X_0=1,C_0=j)=1/z$，故 $\iota=m/z=1/\bar\mu$；除以强度即为（58.1）。
+
+由 $\rho(B_j)<1$，有 $\lambda M_0^n\mathbf1\to0$，所以任意固定起点之后永远无事件的概率为零；对起点取可数并，排除未来仅有限事件。平稳性把同一有限全零区间界转到过去，也排除过去有限事件。于是定理 56.1 证明中的原位点分割（56.7）适用。将（59.6）的实际 Palm 律及 $\iota=1/\bar\mu$ 代入该式，恰得（58.2）的悬挂推前律。因此实际矩阵输出与 $P_f$ 相同，所有长度、首尾及乘积接缝均由一个 $\theta$ 给出；定理 58.2 的风险结论随同律传递。$\square$

+## 60. 严格超出循环几何输出律的五状态消费者
+
+**命题 60.1（全正非几何间隔的实际五状态律）。** 在定理 59.1 中取两个相位，数据为
+
+$$
+\alpha_0=(1,0,0),\quad
+B_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/2&1/2\\0&2/3&0\\0&0&1/2\end{pmatrix},\quad
+b_0=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1/3\\1/2\end{pmatrix},
+\tag{60.1}
+$$
+
+$$
+\alpha_1=(1,0),\quad
+B_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&3/4\end{pmatrix},\quad
+b_1=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1/4\end{pmatrix}.
+\tag{60.2}
+$$
+
+按状态次序 $(R_0,U_0,V_0,R_1,U_1)$，$M_0=\operatorname{diag}(B_0,B_1)$，$M_1$ 仅有
+
+$$
+M_1(U_0,R_1)=1/3,\quad M_1(V_0,R_1)=1/2,\quad M_1(U_1,R_0)=1/4.
+\tag{60.3}
+$$
+
+它的原平稳行、强度及两种间隔为
+
+$$
+\lambda=\frac1{17}(2,3,2,2,8),\quad z=17/2,\quad\iota=4/17,
+\tag{60.4}
+$$
+
+$$
+f_0(g)=\frac16(2/3)^{g-2}+\frac14(1/2)^{g-2},\qquad
+f_1(g)=\frac14(3/4)^{g-2}\quad(g\ge2).
+\tag{60.5}
+$$
+
+该 $\theta\in\Theta_5$ 的可见律有完整合法有限支撑、双半线可恢复约化标记及原风险 $d(P_\theta)=0$。它既不是 iid 间隔更新律，也不等于第 9–15 节任意有限周期循环几何族的任何可见输出律。
+
+**证明。** 两个 $B_j$ 的谱半径分别为 $2/3,3/4$，$\alpha_jb_j=0$，全部定理 59.1 条件成立。由一条强制零后在两个支路等待，直接计算（60.5）。其均值为 $\mu_0=1+(3+2)/2=7/2$、$\mu_1=1+4=5$，故 $z=17/2$，而 $\alpha_0R_0=(1,3/2,1)$、$\alpha_1R_1=(1,4)$ 给（60.4）。例如平稳行发出的两种相位事件流各为 $2/17=1/z$，与（59.6）一致。所有隐藏状态沿正边相通，等待自环也为正，因而此表示还不可约且非周期；这些附加性质不用于一般定理。
+
+两种间隔全正，且 $f_0(2)=5/12\ne1/4=f_1(2)$，所以真实约化周期为二。定理 58.2 给出完整支撑、两个方向各自可见及零风险。在实际 Palm 律下，令 $Y_k=\mathbf1_{\{G_k=2\}}$；两相位均匀且条件独立交替，故
+
+$$
+\operatorname{Cov}_{Q_f}(Y_0,Y_1)
+=\frac5{12}\frac14-\left(\frac{5/12+1/4}{2}\right)^2
+=-\frac1{144}.
+\tag{60.6}
+$$
+
+因此实际 Palm 间隔不是 iid，也就不是 iid 更新输出律。
+
+为排除整个旧循环几何输出族，比较仅由可见 Palm 间隔律定义的内在条件分布。记 $\mathcal G_-=\sigma(G_k:k\le-1)$。定理 58.2 的左半线解码使 $c_0$ 为 $\mathcal G_-$ 可测；给定 $c_0$ 的两侧条件独立性给出
+
+$$
+Q_f(G_0=g\mid\mathcal G_-)=f_{c_0}(g)\quad(g\ge2).
+\tag{60.7}
+$$
+
+具体地，先对任一有限过去间隔柱及固定 $c_0$ 用（58.9）验证积分恒等式，再由可测单调类扩到整个 $\mathcal G_-$；这并非对只观察有限过去时的混合分布作断言。

+对于第 9–15 节任何循环几何律，引理 10.2–10.3 的完整乘积及第 11 节的左解码器同样使其（60.7）右侧几乎处处为某个移位几何分布 $a(1-a)^{g-2}$。常数周期分支本来就是 iid 几何，也满足此性质。任一这种几何分布 $h$ 均满足 $h(2)h(4)-h(3)^2=0$。但此例有
+
+$$
+f_0(2)=5/12,\quad f_0(3)=17/72,\quad f_0(4)=59/432,\qquad
+f_0(2)f_0(4)-f_0(3)^2=1/864>0.
+\tag{60.8}
+$$
+

+## 61. 数学供应、增量及保留的未决桥梁
+
+**约定 61.1（引用与结论范围）。** 第 55–57 节把一个原中心插入对应的一次、两次事件输运，接到同一实际外部胞元及其 Palm 权重；（56.2）复用 [Universal 卷][U] 定理 2.2 的原调和缺陷供应，条件 Jensen 是经典工具。有限像集封闭、不可约性与交换置换的计算仅作为此实际带障碍的分类证明步骤，不构成对任意隐藏生产者的商构造。
+
+第 58 节相对第 9–15 节扩充了分布词，并以单点概率指纹代替正前缀比值，因而允许缺失间隔、有限支撑及概率零、一。它不重证既有几何定理。整数悬挂及 iid 更新识别复用 [更新闭包卷][CG-R] 定义 2.1、引理 2.2；一致常数 $C_{\mathcal R}<c_\star$ 只来自其定理 7.1。有限非负相位型间隔在 [统一更新卷][CG-F] 引理 3.3 已用于 iid 更新；第 59–60 节消费它来给出循环非 iid 的同一有限生产者及严格的可见输出律分离。
+
+[Marzen–Crutchfield][CG-MC] §II.1、§III、§V 与附录 A 处理离散更新过程、方向因果状态，以及有限非单义生产者与无限预测状态的区别；有限生成不供应这里的双可观察标记。[Ellison–Mahoney–Crutchfield][CG-EMC] §II、§V、§VII 的预测、回溯及双向机器是经典相关结构，双向机器的集合转移仍可非单义，不能替代（55.3）、（55.6）的共同标记假设。[Dawid–Lauritzen–Parry][CG-DLP] §4.2、例 4.4、式（14）给条件 Brier／ratio matching 背景，其严格正乘积样本空间不替换这里的硬 no11 纤维及零质量约定。这些引用供应经典方法及相邻概念；第 56–60 节的原风险连接是上述明确前提下的本仓推导，不作文献优先权主张。
+
+**约定 61.2（完整原域仍未决）。** （58.5）是定义 58.1 的整个循环独立间隔类的一致上界，包括其常数更新分支及第 59 节的有限实现。它没有被延伸到一般空间时钟核 $T_g=U^g$、其他相位依赖律或整个 $\Theta_N$。这里没有统一的有限解码半径、速率、任意有限块擦除恢复、最小隐藏维数或对所有参数共用零集的结论。任意有限均值分布也没有被声称为相位型。
+
+一般有限隐藏达到候选是否具有假设 55.2 的同律标记、双侧解码及确定更新，仍缺证明。即使这些假设成立且得到（57.2），其概率核也未被迫为几何；在（56.13）下的标量乘积带约束仍仅为必要条件。故原二择一（54.1）保持原样，包含零平稳坐标、结构零、可约性、周期性及冗余表示的一切 $\Theta_N$ 仍未被本增补决定。上述结论为所列供应与假设下的普通数学证明。
